prompt:
You are the ORCHESTRATOR of a 3-agent team. You will not do the task yourself.
Split the task below into exactly 3 subtasks that can be worked in parallel by 3 agents who each see the
same shared input but only their own subtask instruction. Later you will see all 3 of their outputs and
assemble the final answer yourself, so split the work where the pieces will recombine.

TASK: formalize the claim below as a Lean 4 theorem that COMPILES, and prove it.

THE CLAIM IN ENGLISH
For a body in steady gliding flight, lift balances weight only at or above the minimum airspeed v_min = sqrt(2 * m * g / (rho * S * CLmax)), where m is mass, g gravitational acceleration, rho air density, S lifting area and CLmax the maximum lift coefficient. It follows that of two gliders with the same CLmax and the same air density, the one with the greater wing loading m/S strictly requires the greater minimum airspeed.

REQUIRED CONTENT. A statement that compiles but does not carry these is a failure:
  [1] a square root appears
  [2] the factor 2 appears
  [3] air density is hypothesised positive
  [4] lifting area is hypothesised positive
  [5] the lift coefficient is hypothesised positive
  [6] a STRICT inequality is the conclusion (not a non-strict one)
  [7] two gliders are compared, or wing loading m/S is formed

KNOWN TRAP: A statement that merely defines v_min and proves 0 <= v_min is TRUE and VACUOUS. The strict monotonicity in m/S is the content.

HARD REQUIREMENTS ON THE FILE
- The file starts with exactly `import Mathlib` and imports nothing else. No `open` of a project namespace.
- The main theorem is named exactly `l2_t1`.
- A second declaration named exactly `l2_t1_witness` proves that the hypotheses of `l2_t1` are
  SATISFIABLE by concrete numbers, in the shape `theorem <name>_witness : ∃ ..., <the hypotheses> := by norm_num`
  (an existential over concrete values, proved, not asserted). Without it the theorem may be vacuously true.
- No `sorry`, no `admit`, no `axiom`, no `native_decide`, no `@[implemented_by]`.
- The hypotheses must be LOAD-BEARING: if the conclusion is provable with the hypotheses deleted, the
  formalization is worthless and will be scored as a failure.
- Toolchain: Lean 4 v4.35.0 with Mathlib v4.35.0. Use `Real`, `Real.sqrt`, `positivity`, `nlinarith`,
  `field_simp`, `norm_num` and the Mathlib `Real.sqrt_*` lemmas as you need them. Keep proofs short and robust.

Output the whole file as `lean_file`, the main theorem signature as `statement_only`, and your `notes`.

subtasks.title: Draft the statement and witness
subtasks.instruction: Write the Lean 4 file header and the two declarations WITHOUT proofs of l2_t1 (use the proof slot as a placeholder you clearly mark). File starts with exactly `import Mathlib`, no other imports, no `open` of project namespaces. Suggested statement: theorem l2_t1 (m1 m2 S rho g CL : ℝ) (hrho : 0 < rho) (hS : 0 < S) (hCL : 0 < CL) (hg : 0 < g) (hm1 : 0 < m1) (hwl : m1 / S < m2 / S) : Real.sqrt (2 * m1 * g / (rho * S * CL)) < Real.sqrt (2 * m2 * g / (rho * S * CL)). Adjust if needed so all hypotheses are load-bearing (positivity of rho, S, CL, g and m1 must all be genuinely needed or at least be present; check that deleting them breaks the conclusion where possible, e.g. g>0 and rho,S,CL>0 are needed). Also write `theorem l2_t1_witness : ∃ (m1 m2 S rho g CL : ℝ), <exact same hypotheses as l2_t1 as a conjunction> := by norm_num` using concrete numbers such as m1=1,m2=2,S=1,rho=1,g=1,CL=1 (use ⟨1,2,1,1,1,1, by norm_num⟩ style only if plain `norm_num` cannot close it; the required shape is `:= by norm_num`, so supply the witnesses via `refine ⟨1,2,1,1,1,1,?_⟩; norm_num` only if bare norm_num fails). Output the complete file text and the statement_only signature. If a Lean toolchain is available locally, try compiling.

subtasks.title: Prove l2_t1
subtasks.instruction: Produce a short, robust Lean 4 (Mathlib, Real) proof of: theorem l2_t1 (m1 m2 S rho g CL : ℝ) (hrho : 0 < rho) (hS : 0 < S) (hCL : 0 < CL) (hg : 0 < g) (hm1 : 0 < m1) (hwl : m1 / S < m2 / S) : Real.sqrt (2 * m1 * g / (rho * S * CL)) < Real.sqrt (2 * m2 * g / (rho * S * CL)). Plan: from hwl and hS get m1 < m2 (e.g. `div_lt_div_iff_of_pos_right hS` or `(div_lt_div_iff_of_pos_right hS).mp hwl`, or by_contra + div_le_div_of_nonneg_right); apply Real.sqrt_lt_sqrt (needs 0 ≤ the first argument, by positivity) with the argument inequality proved via div_lt_div_of_pos_right / `by apply div_lt_div_of_pos_right _ (by positivity); nlinarith`. Give two or three fallback variants in case lemma names differ in current Mathlib (e.g. Real.sqrt_lt_sqrt, Real.sqrt_lt_sqrt_iff, gcongr). Return the proof body text and note any lemma names you are unsure of. If a Lean toolchain is available, compile it.

subtasks.title: Audit against requirements and traps
subtasks.instruction: Independently review the following candidate formalization against the checklist, and propose improvements: theorem l2_t1 (m1 m2 S rho g CL : ℝ) (hrho : 0 < rho) (hS : 0 < S) (hCL : 0 < CL) (hg : 0 < g) (hm1 : 0 < m1) (hwl : m1 / S < m2 / S) : Real.sqrt (2 * m1 * g / (rho * S * CL)) < Real.sqrt (2 * m2 * g / (rho * S * CL)). Checklist: [1] sqrt appears; [2] factor 2 appears; [3] rho>0 hypothesis; [4] S>0; [5] CL>0; [6] strict inequality conclusion; [7] two gliders / wing loading m/S formed. Also check: file starts exactly with `import Mathlib`; main theorem named l2_t1; witness named l2_t1_witness of shape `theorem l2_t1_witness : ∃ ..., <same hypotheses> := by norm_num` with concrete numbers and hypotheses matching l2_t1 exactly (note that bare norm_num may not instantiate existential witnesses; suggest a robust form that still ends in norm_num, e.g. `⟨1,2,1,1,1,1, by norm_num⟩` vs `by refine ⟨...⟩ <;> norm_num`); no sorry/admit/axiom/native_decide/implemented_by; hypotheses are load-bearing (say which are genuinely needed; e.g. is hm1 needed, and is it better to state v_min via a def or inline? Prefer inline or a def in the same file, with no project namespace opened). Consider whether the statement should also express the lift-balance part of the claim (v >= v_min iff lift >= weight) and say whether adding it is worth the risk; recommend the minimal safe version. Output a verdict, a list of concrete edits, and a final recommended statement_only signature plus notes text for the final answer.
